// name: Scoped @applyy (TWO y's) per the naming standard; only the repo folder is applyyy. Sibling of @applyy/master-ingest and @applyy/master-pdf.
name: @applyy/master-robots
// version: Workspace-internal only; nothing here is ever published to a registry.
// private: This repo carries resume and CTC data — an accidental `pnpm publish` must be impossible.
// type: ESM only. The gate must be importable by a Deno Edge Function, the Node worker and the browser alike, and Deno cannot consume CommonJS.
// exports: Source-only export map pointing at .ts, exactly like master-ingest, master-pdf and resume-template. No build step: a compiled copy would be a second place the decision table lives, and the whole point of this package is that the robots decision is made in exactly one place.
// types: Redundant with exports for modern resolvers; kept for editors that still read this field.
// files: Only src ships if this is ever packed.
// scripts.typecheck: tsc is a checker only in this repo — noEmit is inherited from tsconfig.base.json.
// scripts.test: The glob is REQUIRED. `node --test test` (a bare directory) fails on Node 24 with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and that error reads exactly like missing fixtures, which has already cost two previous sessions time in master-ingest and master-pdf.
// dependencies: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, AND IT MUST STAY THAT WAY. This is not tidiness — it is what lets `node --test` run this package with an empty root node_modules and no install, which is how it was verified. The moment a workspace dependency is added, the tests stop running without a lockfile-touching install, and the gate that guards every outbound fetch becomes the hardest package in the repo to check. The fetch transport is an INJECTED STRUCTURAL SEAM (see src/fetch.ts RobotsFetcher) rather than an import, specifically so this stays true. src/fetch.ts has ONE cross-tree import — supabase/functions/_shared/http/retry-after.ts — which is a pure, dependency-free function reused rather than copied so the Date.parse("-5") trap has exactly one implementation; it is a relative path, not a package dependency, and adds nothing to install.
// devDependencies: @types/node is needed by the TESTS ONLY (node:test, node:assert). src/ uses no Node API at all — it relies only on fetch, URL, TextEncoder, AbortSignal and RegExp, every one of which exists in Node 24, Deno 2 and the browser. typescript for standalone type-checking; the floor is 5.8 because tsconfig.base.json sets erasableSyntaxOnly, which 5.6/5.7 reject as an unknown option. NOTE: these explanations live at the TOP level because pnpm validates dependency names and rejects a "// x" pseudo-key inside dependencies with ERR_PNPM_INVALID_DEPENDENCY_NAME.
